title: Data policy and model eligibility
summary: Decides which providers may receive internal and confidential data, and whether host prompt logging stays off.

questions.prompt: Which models may receive internal data?

options.label: Approved cloud providers on paid, no-training terms
options.tradeoff: Keeps routing flexible across providers; requires paid API tiers and trust in provider terms.

options.label: One approved provider
options.tradeoff: One contract to audit; no cross-provider routing for internal data.

options.label: Local models only
options.tradeoff: Nothing leaves the machine; only some hosts can reach local models and quality is lower.

questions.prompt: Which provider is the approved one?
Does confidential data require a zero-data-retention endpoint?

options.label: No: confidential data goes where internal data may go
options.tradeoff: Works without a retention agreement; the class stays distinct for audit and path rules.

options.label: Yes: only zero-data-retention or local models
options.tradeoff: Strongest guarantee; confidential steps go to a human until a provider is recorded with zero data retention.

options.label: No confidential class
options.tradeoff: Fewer classes to maintain; confidential-looking data is handled as restricted.

questions.prompt: When is host prompt and content logging disabled?

options.label: On every host that has a setting for it
options.tradeoff: No prompt content in host telemetry, so no restricted content leaks into it; you lose prompt-level debugging.

options.label: Only on hosts permitted near restricted data
options.tradeoff: Keeps prompt logging on other hosts; relies on the hosts rule being right.

options.label: Leave host defaults
options.tradeoff: No changes; some hosts log prompts unless told not to.

decisions.title: Internal data goes only to approved cloud providers on paid no-training terms
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models and to anthropic, openai and google on their paid API tiers. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Internal data goes only to {{answer.provider}} and local models
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models and to {{answer.provider}} on its paid API tier. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Internal data stays on local models
decisions.body:
## Decision

Internal data may go to local models only. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

Providers count as approved only on their paid API tier; free tiers may train on content. Routing removes every model of another provider before it compares cost (guardrail routing-governance-before-cost). Add providers or local models by a new decision or a fact carrying `go-getter.models`.

## Why

Routing for cost must never move data outside the boundary its class allows (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Confidential data may go wherever internal data may
decisions.body:
## Decision

Confidential data goes to the models internal data may go to. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Confidential data requires zero data retention
decisions.body:
## Decision

Confidential data goes only to local models and to providers recorded with zero data retention. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: There is no confidential data class
decisions.body:
## Decision

The project has no confidential class; confidential-looking data is handled as restricted. (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Confidential data needs a retention guarantee only some teams have contracted (decision 0018).

decisions.title: Host prompt logging is disabled on every host
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter apply` switches off prompt and content logging in every host setting that has one (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A host that logs prompts by default would copy restricted content into its telemetry (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Host prompt logging must stay disabled

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given host telemetry can export prompt content, a restricted path read once would leave the machine through logs, so the setting must be off wherever the host exposes it.

enforcement.check: Host settings files that exist have prompt logging switched off

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Keep prompt and content logging disabled in host settings; `go-getter apply` sets it and the check fails when a settings file turns it back on.

decisions.title: Host prompt logging is disabled on hosts permitted near restricted data
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter apply` switches off prompt and content logging on the hosts permitted near restricted data (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Prompts on those hosts may contain restricted content (decision 0018).

guardrails.title: Host prompt logging must stay disabled on hosts near restricted data

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given host telemetry can export prompt content, hosts that may handle restricted data must not log it.

enforcement.check: Settings files of hosts permitted near restricted data have prompt logging switched off

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Keep prompt and content logging disabled on hosts permitted near restricted data; `go-getter apply` sets it and the check fails when a settings file turns it back on.

decisions.title: Host prompt logging keeps host defaults
decisions.body:
## Decision

Host prompt and content logging settings are left as the hosts ship them (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project accepted the leak risk of default prompt logging.
